judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-B lets the Publisher appoint and remove foremen at will while 4-A.1(a) places foremen on Union seniority lists — a structural tension around the foreman's dual status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clean prohibitions; the qualifier 'in accordance with this agreement' is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-G gives the Publisher a complaint route if the Union penalises a foreman, matching this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception clause limiting foremen's performance of Section 2 operations is long but concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Individually negotiated foreman terms sit awkwardly with 4-A.1(a) listing foremen on seniority lists and with 2-K's ban on non-covered persons performing unit work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific supervision requirement keyed to morning/evening papers; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6-D and 3-I's right to operate either shift.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, one requirement; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 6-A.1 and 6-C; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'make changes in operating procedures' is broad, but the clause is a channelling rule rather than a grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 forbids any change in condition without the other party's consent, which limits the foreman's power to change procedures asserted here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'other unfair treatment' is a general catch-all after enumerated specifics (conduct, orders, discrimination).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15 provides a parallel grievance route for employees, and 16-A imposes a 30-day filing limit that this clause does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'improperly imposed penalties' is the only open term, and it mirrors the prohibition in 6-A.2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 6-A.2 and the Section 16 machinery; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or days observed as such' is undefined, and the 'trips' forfeiture turns on obtaining employment 'elsewhere in the industry', a term defined only in 4-A.2(i).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7-C, 7-D, 7-E and 20-D each qualify holiday entitlement differently, and 7-C's sick-leave carve-out adds a further layer to reconcile.
